officialName: Bantam Tools Desktop PCB Milling Machine
description: The Bantam Tools Desktop PCB Milling Machine is a small benchtop CNC mill. In a makerspace, students use it to mill prototype circuit boards from FR-1 copper-clad blanks. They also use it to engrave or cut small parts from machining wax, plastics, wood and soft metals such as aluminium and brass. It has a 5.5 × 4.5 in (140 × 114 mm) working area and holds cutting tools with a 1/8 in shank.

specs.label: Tool holding
specs.value: ER-11 collet; largest recommended shank 1/8 in

specs.label: Minimum PCB trace width and spacing
File input
specs.value: EAGLE BRD (.brd), Gerber RS-274X (.gtl, .grb), G-code (.nc, .tap), SVG (.svg)

specs.label: Power
specs.value: 100-240 V AC 50/60 Hz 1.4 A; 50 W typical / 120 W peak

useRestrictions: Use only with all safety windows in place and the material firmly fixed to the bed, never leave it running unattended, and never use cutting fluid, coolant or unsupported materials such as steel.
